result.title: $R^2$: Recognizing and Reducing Redundant Visual Tool Use
result.summary: Recent studies have shown that visual tools can improve multimodal reasoning. However, the effects of tools vary substantially across samples, and benchmark accuracy alone does not reveal whether tool interactions are beneficial or redundant. We present $R^2$, a framework that recognizes and reduces redundant visual tool use in vision-language models. We first introduce a sample-level Category Analysis of Tool Utility (CAT), which categorizes samples according to whether a model can benefit from tools. This analysis reveals that benchmark scores may obscure a model's tool-use ability. Across seven benchmarks, samples benefiting from tools account for at most 12.44% of each benchmark, while the majority gain little from tool interaction or are even harmed by it. To assess individual calls, we propose the Visual Feedback Dependency (VFD) metric, which compares the likelihood of the same subsequent reasoning under actual and alternative visual feedback without an external evaluator or trajectory regeneration. Redundancy-Aware GRPO (RA-GRPO) combines this dependency signal with a category-conditioned base call cost to assign relative efficiency advantages among correct trajectories, supplementing outcome-based supervision. Across the seven benchmarks, RA-GRPO reduces the mean number of tool calls by 12.39% relative to Vanilla GRPO at comparable benchmark accuracy. Evaluated by tool-utility category, RA-GRPO improves category macro-average accuracy over Vanilla GRPO by 3.35 percentage points.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 R² 框架，用于识别并减少 VLM 中冗余的视觉工具调用：先用样本级工具效用分类（CAT）发现七个基准中最多仅 12.44% 的样本真正受益于工具，再提出 Visual Feedback Dependency 指标评估单次调用的依赖程度，并用 RA-GRPO 将依赖信号与调用成本结合入训练，在精度相当下减少约 12% 的工具调用。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中「LOOK 的收益是否真实、何时停止」问题：其 CAT 分解与 VFD 依赖度量可供核查单次视觉证据调用的因果贡献与成本权衡；需注意其重点是调用冗余与训练奖励设计，而非 latent 状态的内部表示。
